subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should OpenClaw require runtime untrusted-content handling for gh-issues plus per-spawn child tool scoping before this issue can close, or accept prompt-level guidance and global subagent policy as sufficient hardening?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent boundary affects model-facing skill execution, sessions_spawn public API shape, child session policy state, and SECURITY.md vulnerability-versus-hardening semantics.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
options.body: Land or replace the open toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, or equivalent runtime isolation before treating this fixed.

options.title: Accept prompt-only hardening
options.body: Treat a narrower SKILL.md policy update as sufficient defense-in-depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain inside the operator-granted agent trust boundary.

options.title: Defer unified design
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers design one delegated-agent content and capability policy for skills, hooks, cron, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
recommendation.body: Land or replace the open toolsAllow work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, or equivalent runtime isolation before treating this fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: The public review trail and related sessions_spawn policy discussions point to Peter for the API/security boundary decision.
